svg.title: agentd - AWS architecture (staging, ap-northeast-1) - verified against the live account, 2026-09-08

g.text: agentd - AWS architecture (staging, ap-northeast-1) - verified against the live account, 2026-09-08
VPC 10.0.0.0/16 - 2 public subnets (1a / 1c), IGW, NO NAT, no private subnets
ECS cluster - 2 x t3.medium, EC2 + bridge, bin-packed
images from ECR - secrets from Secrets Manager - logs to CloudWatch (14d)
Lambdas - outside the VPC (no NAT, so in-VPC has no route to S3)
Supporting - reached by everything, no request path drawn
TLS certificates and log shipping are named inside the boxes.
1. Every subnet is public and all 9 ALB ports face the internet.
There is no NAT, so every task needs a public IP to reach
ECR, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch and Neon.
2. Since the EC2 move, Cloud Map (agentd.local) is EMPTY - it only
publishes A records for awsvpc tasks. So daemon -> accounts,
a check on every request, now hairpins out through the public ALB.
3. The executor is the trust boundary: a marketplace plugin's tools,
an authored agent's Python and the builder's shell all run there,
one microVM per call, never on the daemon that holds every
